title: Pivot station runnotes
content:
Quick notes for tonight's bridge -> pivot handoff. Personal scratchpad, messy — keep what helps you run faster.

TL;DR:
- Prioritize latency alerts for hosted-api (route: /v1/generate) and any error spikes on model-routing service (model-router).
- If batcher gets stuck, try soft-restart (see commands). Avoid full pool recycle during peak unless SRE lead ok.

Active/Recurring items:
1) High p95 on hosted-api -> often KV-cache misses after deploys or when redis-green pods restart. Warm cache before traffic surge: run kv-warmup script (below).
2) Dedicated pool scaleup stalls -> autoscaler sometimes fails to attach GPUs when nodes in PROXY state (INFRA-3245). Manual intervene: drain node, force restart pod agent, then uncordon.
3) Intermittent 503s from private deployments in eu-west-1: networking team investigating - root cause often transient iptables rule on bastion. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-4311.

Useful commands (copy/paste):
- Check hosted-api latency dashboards: https://observability.redwood.example/dashboards/hosted-api
- Quick health: curl -sS -X GET "https://api.redwood.example/health" | jq
- Check model-router pods: kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-router
- Tail logs: kubectl -n serving logs deploy/model-router -f --tail=200
- Warm KV cache (small sample): python tools/kv_warmup.py --model gpt-small --routes 50 --rate 20
- Soft-restart batcher: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deploy/batcher (gives in-place reconnects)
- Force GPU agent restart (last resort): systemctl restart gpu-agent.service on node (ssh as coreops)

Playbook snippets (for common incidents):
A) p95 latency spike on /v1/generate (>1.2s sustained 5m):
  - Check batching backlog: kubectl -n serving exec deploy/batcher -- /bin/sh -c "redis-cli LLEN batch_queue" (if >1000, consider shedding)
  - Check KV cache hit rate: curl -sS https://observability/api/kv-metrics | jq '.hit_rate'
  - If hit_rate < 60% after deploy, run kv warmup for top 10 routes: python tools/kv_warmup.py --preset top10
  - If batcher backlog continues and autoscaler isn't adding pods: kubectl -n serving get hpa; check autoscaler logs (kubectl logs deploy/autoscaler)
  - Escalation: page oncall-eng (s-reliable) if retries > 3 and customer-impacting.

B) Dedicated pool scale failure (new nodes stuck PROXY/NotReady):
  - Verify node events: kubectl describe node <node-name>
  - Check agent logs on the host: journalctl -u gpu-agent -n 400
  - Common quick fix: restart agent, then kubectl uncordon <node-name>. If agent fails repeatedly, open INFRA ticket and attach agent logs.
  - Workaround: shift traffic to fallback pool via routing policy: POST to /admin/routing/policy with body: {"route":"model-x","fallback":"cpu-small"} (ops-only, use curl + token)

C) 502/503 volume from private deployment in eu-west-1:
  - Check customer control plane connectivity: curl -I https://priv-cp-eu.example/status
  - If control plane unreachable, check VPN/bastion status (ssh to jump host and run ./net-check.sh)
  - Escalate to networking (tag: @netops) if bastion shows iptables changes in last 30m.

Notes to self / TODOs (handy for next shift):
- Add a shorter kv-warmup mode (5 routes) and expose as scheduled job for pre-peak. (Ticket idea: PROPOSAL-kwarm-001)
- Document exact thresholds we want for batcher shed vs autoscale in product doc. Right now it's fuzzy and causes hesitation during incidents.
- Revisit the restart play for batcher: rollout restart vs pod delete — one is less disruptive for KV connections.

Recent incidents summary (last 72h):
- 2026-03-09 03:14 UTC: p95 spike (hosted-api) -> root cause: redis-green pod OOM; fixed by increasing memory and warming cache. (see github PR #512)
- 2026-03-10 21:40 UTC: Dedicated pool attach failure -> reverted recent node image; follow-up INFRA-3245 assigned to Marisol.

Escalation contacts (fast):
- Oncall Eng (primary): @oncall-eng (room: #oncall)
- SRE lead (pager): Liam O'Connor
- GPU infra (pager): Marisol Vega
- NetOps: netops@redwood.example (for private deployments)

Housekeeping for handoff:
- Leave this doc updated with any commands you used and any new artifacts (PRs / tickets).
- If you open an incident, paste the runbook summary back here for the next person.

Random helpful snippets I've pasted before:
- To temporarily route traffic from host A to B (admin token required):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","target":"fallback-small"}' https://admin.redwood.example/routing

- When in doubt, warm the KV cache for the specific model variant experiencing misses — it's faster than draining and often reduces p95 by 30-60ms.

Questions to follow-up on tomorrow (notes for oncall triage):
- Can we get automated pre-warm for top 5 routes when new model version deploys? (reduce friction)
- Is there a safe way to mark a node as temporarily ineligible for autoscaler without full cordon?

End of scratchpad. Keep this for tonight's shift and then move any sensible bits into the confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.example/ops/oncall-runbooks/pivot-station (I will tidy later).

-- Rhea
